set.body:
Reuse bd-01M02N4EKAEA6EBB3TE0G4TYMP (psychology-facing workflow facade and task-first documentation). Add comparative first-use acceptance rather than a second facade.

Acceptance:
- A clean installation and short executable guide take a researcher from accessible example data to quality assessment, events/measures, a useful figure, tidy export and a saved/reloaded analysis. Name necessary geometry, timing and scientific parameters without making the reader learn internal registries or the full architecture.
- Evaluate the same task against pinned pymovements with a predeclared rubric: installation/setup success, unaided task completion, task time, errors/recovery, discoverability and explanation burden. Record participant background and small-sample limitations; lines of code and agent walkthroughs alone do not establish researcher usability.
- Demonstrate a meaningful improvement in the declared primary usability outcome, with no material regression in task success or scientific transparency. Freeze the practical thresholds before evaluation; retain unsuccessful attempts.
- Familiar defaults remain typed, visible and inspectable. Diagnostics name operands and recovery actions. Examples compile/run from public artifacts, and docs accurately state actual support, limitations and platform requirements.
- Correct stale competitor descriptions (pymovements carries Screen/Experiment metadata and uses Polars), stale detector README claims and other factual drift encountered in these journeys. Distinguish architectural elegance from ease of completing work.

Split facade repairs or additional journey work into bounded owned slices. Reuse existing docs/consumer checks and Studio usability evidence where the task and population match.
set.title: PM2: make first use and the public API demonstrably easier
